Exempts detached runner jobs from the quoted night-heartbeat and night-stall-guard non-goals; amends no numbered D- or O-decision and supersedes no ADR.\n* Review: maintainer chose the direction on 2026-11-24 (`decisions.md` Q-1–Q-7) · Decider: maintainer · prepared by Codex.\n* Date: 2026-11-24 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nResearch on 2026-11-23 found that runner child groups are tied to their launching session and the report does not prove job survival (`plans/changes/detached-job-launcher/research.md`, run 28bf813a). Earlier night-run changes excluded headless jobs; the interview on 2026-11-24 chose a different boundary.\n\n## Decision Drivers\n\n* Jobs survive session exit and can be observed live.\n* Verification retains one machine-wide admission and job outcomes remain visible.\n* The launcher can travel with the kit across harnesses.\n\n## Considered Options\n\n* A separate tmux window per job and durable records: live observation and survival require tmux.\n* A separate process session: fewer prerequisites, but live observation needs another mechanism.\n* A launchd job: host-specific service supervision with additional platform coupling.\n\n## Decision\n\nChosen option: a separate tmux window per job with durable records, because it provides survival and live observation across harnesses. `scripts/jobs.py` starts, lists and stops jobs; model calls remain routed through `scripts/stage2.py`. Verification uses the existing admission. Job records live beside runner state and the report reads them. The launcher does not write lane or busy markers. The existing 30-minute wake remains until `lanes.py advance` lands. The earlier non-goals read: night-heartbeat, “A new scheduler, daemon, model call, notification service or automatic restart of an unavailable session; delivery uses the harness's existing scheduling or background-completion facility”; night-stall-guard, “A scheduler, daemon, headless heartbeat architecture, automatic restart, lane planner, runner process watchdog, dashboard or notification service.” night-heartbeat also excludes “Runner process supervision, recap-lock repair, tracker lease renewal, new concurrency limits or new permission to merge or start work.” Only detached `scripts/stage2.py` runner verbs and `make verify` jobs are exempted from those quoted non-goals; all other detached commands remain under them, and a scheduler, daemon and automatic restart remain excluded. Every runner verb and `make verify` must use the launcher; harness background mode remains available for commands outside the runner.\n\n## Consequences\n\n* tmux is a prerequisite and missing tmux is reported before launch.\n* A durable record and log must outlive the window and correctly represent unknown outcomes.\n* Detached jobs may wait for the shared verification admission.\n\n## Validation\n\n* The change's tests exercise session exit, status, stopping, reporting and shared verification admission; `make verify` runs before phase 6.\n* A real tmux run and review of the updated night-run guidance confirm the decision before merge.\n",

          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "citation": "docs/architecture/2026-09-17-omnigent-first-target.md::Outcome and boundaries",
          "end_line": 118,
          "excerpt": "## Outcome and boundaries\n\n- **The promise.** A developer turns an agreed change into a reviewable pull\n  request — through bounded workers, reproducible checks and an independent\n  review.\n- **Interruption is safe.** A fresh session resumes from a durable checkpoint,\n  without the previous chat.\n- **Who owns what.** Omnigent owns dispatch and observation. Git holds the\n  change and its evidence. Beads holds work status. The human owns intent,\n  exceptions and the final merge.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    H[\"Human\"] -- \"intent, exceptions, final merge\" --> C[\"Omnigent coordinator\"]\n    C -- \"dispatch, observation\" --> W[\"2 coding workers, bounded sessions\"]\n    W -- \"commits\" --> G[\"Git: change + evidence\"]\n    C -- \"accepted outcomes\" --> T[\"Beads: work status\"]\n    G -- \"candidate branch\" --> P[\"Reviewed PR to main\"]\n```\n\n- **Harness vs instances.** The harness owns reusable process and its kit.\n  Instances own domain rules, endpoint permissions, secrets and additional\n  gates.\n- **Customer boundary.** Customer expressions never enter harness artefacts.\n- **Language.** Content, commit messages and PR bodies are English.\n- **Naming amendment (D-17).** The proposed public scan permits tool names\n  such as Omnigent and LikeC4; it rejects customer/employer identifiers and\n  secrets. Model selection stays in routing configuration. This amendment\n  does not postpone public-readiness work.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Free swarm, paid Flash swarm, then single paid rungs until\nclean\", because it implements the maintainer's recorded answers, including\nthe corrected order and automatic free admission.\n\n1. **Clean ends the loop at every round number.** A completed round is clean\n   once every row is decided and none has Status beginning `taken` or\n   `fixed`; no rows or all rejected rows count. A clean free round ends the\n   loop before any paid review. This amends ADR 0011 decision 3's compulsory\n   second round, three-round cap and special round-3 admission rule.\n2. **Round 1 is the discovered free Go swarm.** Before each fresh loop run,\n   the runner forces `tools/pi/pi update --models` in its scratch agent\n   directory, then reads `tools/pi/pi --list-models` there. Failed/timed-out\n   refresh refuses before listing or model calls; no stale-cache fallback.\n   The YAML rule holds provider (initially `opencode-go`), id suffix\n   (initially `-free`), and include/exclude lists with date and reason per\n   entry. Include only ids present under the configured Go provider in that\n   catalog; exclusions win. Never admit provider `opencode` (Zen). All\n   selected ids enter without individual declarations; no free id/suffix\n   literal belongs in runner code. Invalid rules, unreadable/empty selection\n   or failed listing refuse the run. Record UTC check time, source `pi.dev`,\n   Pi version, rule, catalog and selected ids. Changes apply to fresh runs\n   through an ordinary YAML PR. State the live intermediary and unmeasured\n   free billing explicitly.\n3. **The free class is declared and confined.** The endpoint entry declares\n   this class and the accepted unread retention/training terms (Q-8/Q-9).\n   Admission requires membership in this run's discovery plus the free-only\n   purpose; it does not relax generic paid or interactive model declarations.\n   Only implementation source/test diff hunks reach these calls, with no\n   repository-reading instructions, tools, context loaders or whole-worktree\n   prompt. Existing per-call declaration and leak checks remain mandatory.\n4. **Round 2 is the parallel paid Flash swarm; later rounds go cheapest first.**\n   The Flash swarm is a hand-kept list (`flash_swarm`) of eligible paid\n   models; the runner never changes it, and prints a notice (and writes one\n   record line) when it is not the three admitted models with the highest\n   `anfragen_5h`. The paid ladder is a set (`modelle`): the runner orders it by\n   a declared cost value, `anfragen_5h` in each model's `modelle_terms` record\n   (the Go page's \"Estimated requests\", Go column, requests per 5 hours, with\n   its reading date and source), descending, ties by id; a model without the\n   value goes last and is named on stderr and in the record (maintainer,\n   2026-10-17, Q-13, replacing the hand-ordered list). Later rounds take one\n   eligible model at a time in that order, Flash members excluded while they\n   are in the swarm. When a Flash member fails (nonzero exit, timeout, empty\n   answer), the runner calls the cheapest admitted ladder model that is not in\n   the round and not consumed, on the same paid prompt; if that one fails,\n   the next, each model at most once, until one answers or the ladder is\n   spent. A replacement is consumed: it is no later rung. Each swap is written\n   `<model> failed: <reason>; replaced by <model>` in the loop record and\n   printed on stderr; the reason carries the last line of Pi's standard\n   error. The configuration holds ids and cost values; all paid calls retain\n   the existing read tools. Q-10 replaces Q-5's round number without changing\n   parallel Flash review. The free stage selects only ids in the freshly\n   fetched `opencode-go` overlay of the forced refresh, not ids only Pi's\n   shipped list carries.\n5. **Paid terms are read before admission.** Record dated retention/training\n   readings for paid models. Retention is read and recorded;\n   training must be \"Not used\".\n   Skip and name in th",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n**(c)**, with these contracts:\n\n* **The architecture delta lives in the change's `design.md`.** A section\n  \"Architecture delta\" holds:\n  1. a Mermaid diagram — a flowchart, the form GitHub renders — of the part\n     of the system the change touches, as it is after the change, each box\n     labelled with its C4 level (person, system, container, component);\n  2. below it, three short lists of elements and relationships: **added**,\n     **changed**, **removed**.\n\n  If nothing architectural moves, one sentence says why.\n* **No model as code in the kit now.** No LikeC4 specification, no `model/`\n  scaffold, no `likec4 build` or `likec4 validate` gate, no Node.js\n  dependency. Elements are named as the existing diagrams and ADRs name\n  them, as in LakeSwitch's D-58.\n* **D-15 is amended.** Its LikeC4 part — the tool, the pinned specification\n  and the build gate — is replaced by the architecture delta. Its arc42 and\n  MADR templates are not touched by this ADR; when the kit ships them stays\n  with the template work.\n* **O-3 is amended in one clause.**\n  * **Kept:** an Architectural change requires an ADR in the same pull\n    request. The ADR duty for architectural changes is unchanged.\n  * **Changed:** \"and a model diff\" becomes \"and a filled 'Architecture\n    delta' section in its `design.md`\".\n  * **Not touched:** the DRIFT rule for a module created, deleted or renamed\n    under `src/` or `spec/` in a change of another class.\n* **LikeC4 stays the upgrade path.** The question returns, as an ADR of its\n  own, when any one of these happens:\n  1. a review records, for the third time, a defect in an Architectural\n     change that a model delta would have caught, and the reviewer names it\n     as such in `findings.md` — LakeSwitch's D-58 trigger, so both\n     repositories move together;\n  2. the same element appears in three or more architecture pictures, and a\n     rename or split had to be made by hand in more than one of them;\n  3. the model grows past about thirty elements — more than one page holds —\n     and an agent's work needs dependency queries across it.\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0014-a-change-claims-its-adr-files.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 147,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism. Each repository\n   records the day it adopted the gate; a change begun on or before that day\n   is exempt from the class minimums and from point 4, never from points 2 and\n   3. Moving that day is a decision pull request.\n\n**How it holds from this change on:**\n\n* The claim is the spec header field `adr_files`; the gate\n  `interview-minimums` (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) holds points 2\n  to 4.\n* The day stands in `decisions/adoption.yaml`, a file that stays in its\n  repository; this repository's day is 2026-10-08, the day it adopted the\n  gate, so no change here moves between stock and subject. The gate reads the\n  day thr",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`).           "excerpt": "# ADR 0008 — A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges the pull request carrying it — no commit signing in Coding Harness\n\n* Status: accepted by the merge of the pull request that carries this file.\n  Until that merge, the pull request's state is the decision's state: open\n  is proposed, closed is rejected. In Coding Harness nothing checked those signatures; the practice\nwas a habit here, described in `docs/how-to/signed-decisions.md`.\n\nThe change that brought the ADR question into Coding Harness\n(`plans/changes/harness-decide-adr/`, bead coding-harness-3ar) made the gap\nconcrete. Every feature now owes the maintainer's answer to the question\n\"does this need an ADR?\", stored in `decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`\nand held by the gate `adr-answers`. That gate can see that an answer exists\nand has the right format. It cannot see whether the maintainer gave it or an\nagent wrote it. The interview of 2026-09-30 first planned a signature check\nas the very next change: a port of the LakeSwitch gate with the fix of its\nkey-list weakness (bead coding-harness-in1) and a recovery for the loss of\nthe only key.\n\nLater the same day the maintainer decided against signing in Coding Harness\naltogether. The signing key lives in the laptop's Secure Enclave, and much\nof the maintainer's work happens from a phone; a decision that can only be\nconfirmed at the laptop waits for the laptop.\n\nTwo facts bound every option:\n\n* Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account. GitHub shows the\n  maintainer as the one who merged, whoever pressed the button.\n* GitHub lets no author approve their own pull request. Under one account,\n  the approval rule of the rule set — whoever approves is neither the author\n  nor the last pusher (rule RB-M2 of `docs/governance/regelwerk.md`) —\n  cannot be met.\n\n## Decision Drivers\n\n* The maintainer can confirm a decision from a phone.\n* An agent may prepare a decision; it never makes one.\n* The confirmation happens where the maintainer already looks: the pull\n  request.\n* One mechanism for every decision file — the paths `provenance.yaml`\n  reserves for `human-decided`: ADRs, ADR answers, the rule set.\n* LakeSwitch can read Coding Harness's answer format unchanged\n  (`schema_version: 1`), whatever it decides about its own signing.\n\n## Considered Options\n\n* (a) **Signed commits, as in LakeSwitch.** A decision takes effect only\n  through a commit the maintainer signs with the Touch-ID key, checked by a\n  port of the LakeSwitch signature gate with a signers file and an anchor\n  commit.           "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. GLM 5.3 Flash explores a `bounded` change or a `spike` (a `feature` or `architectural` change goes to the research swarm, ADR 0020) and implements, and Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes (`repair <change>`, ADR 0017: a fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; phase 6 re-checks in a fresh read-only Codex session — a reviewer's own session never repairs); `explore <change>`, `draft <change>`, `implement <change>` and `repair <change>` are live;\n`--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 and records why when Stage 2 is off or Z.ai unavailable. A leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback. Reviews go by class, and so does phase 1 now (ADR 0020): a `feature` or `architectural` change explores through the research swarm (ADR 0020; a finder trio maps the sources, six seats research eleven topics, online topics on public sources only, Opus 5.5 reconciling; `prepare-explore <change>` first, its report shown to the maintainer, then `explore <change> --availability-reported <id>`; an aborted run resumes; the gate `research-handoff` holds interview and spec to the findings), a `bounded` change or a `spike` through GLM 5.3 Flash; `explore` reads the class from `--class` and the headers of `research.md` and `spec.md`, wherever stated, and refuses missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).           "excerpt": "def read_change(change: str, path: str, text: str, *, source: AttributionSource | None = None) -> ReaderResult:\n    \"\"\"The one read of one change's findings.md — the call every consumer keeps (criterion 6).\"\"\"\n    parsed = parse_findings(text, change=change, path=path)\n    findings, gaps = resolve(attribute_rows(parsed, source=source))\n    return ReaderResult(findings, [*parsed.gaps, *gaps], parsed.outside)\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::read_state",
          "end_line": 5739,
          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::released_cut_rounds",
          "end_line": 5543,
          "excerpt": "def released_cut_rounds(findings_text: str) -> set[int]:\n    \"\"\"The rounds that every released block of findings.md carries as cut.\"\"\"\n    found: set[int] = set()\n    own = False\n    for line in findings_text.splitlines():\n        if line.startswith(\"## \"):\n            own = line.startswith(RELEASE_HEADING)\n        elif KEPT_FROM.match(line):\n            own = False\n        elif own and (match := CUT_ROUNDS_LINE.fullmatch(line)):\n            found.update(int(number) for number in match.group(1).split(\", \"))\n    return found\n",

          "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-24-draft-adr-state-first-and-manifest.md::Decision",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`.           "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`. The lock is advisory, held by the open descriptor, and\n    a descriptor dies with its process - so a crashed run leaves no lock behind to break the next.\n    Supersession holds its own and every selected worktree's lock in one deterministic order, so it\n    cannot bypass a normal user of either record (bead coding-harness-e82i, criterion 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    path = record_base() / f\"{key}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"another run holds the loop record `{key}`; one runner at a time\") from error\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "def replace_record(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write the record whole or not at all: a temporary file in its directory, then an atomic rename\n    (`Path.replace`, which is `os.replace`).\n\n    `Path.write_text` truncates first and writes after; a write that fails between the two keeps a\n    record cut short, and the record is the only copy of its rounds (DL-A-4 of the deep review). The\n    temporary file never outlives a failed write.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    handle, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\", dir=path.parent)\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(handle, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n            stream.write(text)\n            stream.flush()\n            # Reconciliation also replaces findings.md: retain its permissions instead of\n            # installing mkstemp's private mode. Fresh external records keep that private mode.\n            if path.exists():\n                os.fchmod(stream.fileno(), path.stat().st_mode & 0o7777)\n            os.fsync(stream.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "excerpt": "### The review loop (phase 4b)\n\n**Fresh availability-enabled runs (Q-16, ADR 0021):** first run\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-loop <change>`. This acknowledges\nthe report; the runner cannot inspect the conversation UI. The external\nreceipt is bound to the worktree, configuration and diff and expires after\n900 seconds. Changed inputs or failed preparation invalidate it. Preparation\nadds one actual call per tested candidate and is no review-quality or billing\nmeasurement. Up to three cheapest reachable paid candidates dynamically fill\nthe Flash swarm; the remaining reachable paid candidates form the ladder.\nExisting snapshots and legacy declarations without the rule retain the\nbehavior below. A record\nwithout a usable `valid_until` — missing, not a quoted date, or an impossible\ncalendar date — grants no admission, and the runner never infers, extends or\nrenews a date at runtime. A refusal names the model, says whether the expiry\nis missing, invalid or passed, and names the recorded date once it has\npassed. From seven UTC days before expiry through the expiry day,\npreparation and every round — fresh, legacy or resumed — print a warning\nwith the model id and date, and the round's notes carry it, so the released\nfindings keep it; a warning neither admits nor refuses, an expired reading\nis a skip with its reason, not a warning, and a skipped record with a valid\ndate warns too. A saved selection or a fresh receipt does not keep an\nexpired member admissible: the round is refused before the call, and the\nrun's history stands. Renewal is not the runner's: a reading is introduced\nor renewed by an agent's dated source re-read and a decision pull request\nmerged by the maintainer; where the source states an end date it is\nrecorded, and otherwise a record expires `gelesen` plus 30 calendar days.\nMigrated 2026-10-26 on that rule; both DeepSeek readings carry the\ndocumented 2026-10-25 source re-read and expire 2026-10-31.\n\nAfter implementation and before phase 6, `review-loop` runs one round per\ncall, and the loop runs **until a round is clean — every row of a round\ndecided and none accepted (ADR 0021).** Round 1 is the **free swarm**: a\nforced live catalog refresh (`pi update --models` before `pi --list-models`,\nno stale cache listed) discovers the models the `opencode-go` provider offers,\nand the `free_stage` rule in `model-endpoints.yaml` — provider, id suffix,\nincludes, excludes — selects the members; they review in parallel, each with\nno tools, from a scratch directory, and their only input is the\nimplementation diff: bounded hunks of source and test code against the merge\nbase with `origin/main`, uncommitted and untracked code included. The catalog\nis a live intermediary (`pi.dev`): the check proves which catalog was read,\nnot what OpenCode Go bills. The prompt carries the implementation diff up to\nthe shared bound of `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES` (4000 lines); a cut, whether by\nthat bound or by the free stage's own file or total limits, is recorded in the\nround, and a round over a cut diff never counts as clean (R-12, R-15).           "end_line": 90,
          "excerpt": "## Consequences\n\n### Positive\n* `lanes.py`, `jobs.py`, `stage2.py` attempts, and `coding-harness-oebl` share one clean, lock-safe JSON/JSONL persistence pattern.\n* Eliminates Markdown regex state corruption, CRLF/table escaping regressions, and silent missing-import bugs in exported kits.\n* Keeps future multi-language transfer (`TypeScript`, `Rust`, `SQL`, `PySpark`, documented separately as non-normative notes) clean because structured JSON/JSONL state and a single manifest do not hardcode Python prose formats.\n\n### Negative / Migration costs\n* Existing `loop.md` readers and tests require updating in coordinated slices (`coding-harness-5ane.11`, `coding-harness-vg9`).\n* Consolidating `scripts/kit/manifest.yaml` and retiring `scripts/export/manifest.yaml` requires updating `tests/test_kit.py` (including removing `test_the_kit_list_is_not_derivable_from_the_export_list` once one manifest is decided).\n\n",

German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "## Files and sequence\n\n1. Create `scripts/jobs.py` with `start`, `list`, and `stop`; use a unique job ID, preserve command argument boundaries and working directory, and check tmux before starting. Start a detached dedicated `tmux -L coding-harness` server if absent and one window per job with a wrapper independent of the launcher process. Pass the caller cwd and whole environment explicitly per job, clearing `HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD`, `HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_TOKEN`, `HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_ID` and `HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_WAIT`; pass `VIRTUAL_ENV` and the caller PATH including its virtual-environment prefix. Classify as a runner verb when argv invokes scripts/stage2.py followed by a non-option word, without importing stage2. Store a schema-validated, atomically written JSON record including the two PIDs with process start times, process groups and stop request. Pass its path to the command via an environment variable. Wait at most 10 seconds for both PIDs; otherwise exit 1 with state failed to start. The wrapper captures both streams in the job log, waits for the actual command and atomically writes its end time and exit status. Place records and logs under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/jobs/`. A vanished wrapper without a completed record is lost and remains visible until pruning 14 days after start; the wrapper records an exit code or `signal N`. Write the stop request before signalling the selected command tree and recorded process groups, including separately sessioned descendants; after five seconds escalate surviving verified identities to SIGKILL; spare the wrapper to record `signal 15` regardless of exit status, and release admission without touching other jobs. Refuse stop on finished, lost or process-identity-mismatched jobs with exit 2; a reused PID counts as gone. Prune each log with its record; keep finished records 14 days from end and lost records 14 days from start; list running jobs, retained lost jobs and those finished within 24 hours by default, all retained records with `--all`. Refuse malformed records and failed starts clearly; concurrent jobs must not overwrite one another.\n2. Use the existing verification entry point from the job itself, without holding an admission in the short-lived launcher or creating a second quota. Clear all four inherited admission values so every job obtains its own slot; model commands continue through `scripts/stage2.py`. Do not write lane or busy markers. `lanes.py advance` is future work and is not implemented here.\n3. Change `scripts/stage2.py` to append every process group it starts in its own session, with process identity, to the supplied job record. Change `scripts/machine_facts.py` to include job records in its jobs field. Change `scripts/run_report.py` to read the same job records and show running jobs, deduplicate by started command PID against process recognition, show only the program name without arguments for non-runner jobs, and show an explicit unreadable or lost state on bad or incomplete data; retain its existing report and read-only behavior.           "excerpt": "## Boundary\n\nLimits this change accepts; phase 6 judges a row that describes only one of them as that limit (decisions Q-7, phase-6 grammar review of 2026-11-20).\n\n- **The reader reads the grammar in `scripts/findings_reader.py`, not all of Markdown.** Three cases are deliberately not read as a Markdown renderer would: a setext heading whose text spans several lines is labelled by its last line only; rows without a header row above them are read as rows, although a renderer shows them as a paragraph; and HTML blocks other than comments (`<details>`, `<table>`) are not opaque, so a table line inside one is read as a row.\n- **Severity, dimension and origin are measured, not enforced, by the reader.** A non-blank free value (`impl`, `Correctness`) is no gap under criterion 16; the fixed vocabulary is a matter for the new-row gate (decisions Q-7).\n- **A released loop section counts only its first table (decisions Q-8).** The runner's `release-loop` writes one table under each `## Phase 4b — loop rows, released <date>` heading; any further table separated by a blank line under that heading stands outside the count.\n\n",

          "citation": "plans/changes/detached-job-launcher/design.md::Data model",
          "end_line": 40,
          "excerpt": "## Data model\n\nOne schema-validated, atomically published JSON record per generated job ID stores the argument vector, runner-verb classification, working directory, started command PID, wrapper PID, recorded process groups, each PID’s process start time, stop request, window identity, start time, end time, exit code or signal, and log path. The launcher creates it before launch; the wrapper atomically publishes completion. A missing completion is not proof of success: list reports `lost` when the wrapper PID is gone. The launcher passes the record path through the environment; stage2 adds its separately sessioned groups. Stop records its request before ending the command tree and recorded groups, spares the wrapper to record `signal 15`, and refuses finished, lost or identity-mismatched jobs. Finished records are kept 14 days; the default list shows running jobs and the last 24 hours, lost records remain visible until pruned 14 days after start, and `--all` shows all retained records. Start waits at most 10 seconds for both PIDs or records a failed start; the log captures both output streams and is pruned with its record. Distinct IDs and atomic replacement prevent simultaneous jobs from overwriting one another.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Boundary\n\nLimits this change accepts; phase 6 judges a row that describes only one of them as that limit (decisions Q-7, phase-6 grammar review of 2026-11-20).\n\n- **The reader reads the grammar in `scripts/findings_reader.py`, not all of Markdown.** Three cases are deliberately not read as a Markdown renderer would: a setext heading whose text spans several lines is labelled by its last line only; rows without a header row above them are read as rows, although a renderer shows them as a paragraph; and HTML blocks other than comments (`<details>`, `<table>`) are not opaque, so a table line inside one is read as a row.\n- **Severity, dimension and origin are measured, not enforced, by the reader.** A non-blank free value (`impl`, `Correctness`) is no gap under criterion 16; the fixed vocabulary is a matter for the new-row gate (decisions Q-7).\n- **A released loop section counts only its first table (decisions Q-8).** The runner's `release-loop` writes one table under each `## Phase 4b — loop rows, released <date>` heading; any further table separated by a blank line under that heading stands outside the count.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Q-7 · Who enforces the cell vocabulary: the reader or a gate (phase-6 grammar review)\n\nasked: 2026-11-20\nanswer: \"Leser misst, Gate setzt durch\" — the reader measures: severity, dimension and origin need only a non-blank cell, while ID, reviewer and Status stay strict because the count depends on them; historical rows with a free vocabulary are counted again. The gate enforces: the fixed vocabulary (origin `base`, `loop` or `fix-r<N>`, the severity set, the dimension set) applies only to new or changed rows, through the existing new-row gate `scripts/check_finding_duplicates.py`, without a new entry in `decisions/gates.yaml`.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the hand repair of phase-6 rows F6-1 and F6-2, a review of the reader's whole input grammar, found that its cell check rejects real history.\n  Intention: the per-model report must be usable on main; history is protected and cannot be rewritten.\n  Today: at commit faa75a3d the main report had 1555 gaps; 1414 were historical rows whose origin is free text (`impl`, `Phase 6`, a model name), 47 a free dimension, 9 a free severity. The reader half is built; the gate half waits on a follow-up question, because three released loop rows the runner wrote on this branch carry the dimension `Correctness`, and the gate would block runner output that may not be edited by hand.)\n\nIn the context of a per-model report over protected historical findings, facing rows whose severity, dimension or origin is free text although those cells decide no count, we decided that the reader asks only that they are not blank while ID, reviewer and Status stay strict, and that the fixed vocabulary is enforced on new or changed rows by the existing new-row gate, to achieve a report that counts the real history and a vocabulary that holds from now on, accepting that historical rows keep their free vocabulary for good. — 2026-11-20\n\n",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "## Data model\n\nOne schema-validated, atomically published JSON record per generated job ID stores the argument vector, runner-verb classification, working directory, started command PID, wrapper PID, recorded process groups, each PID’s process start time, stop request, window identity, start time, end time, exit code or signal, and log path. The launcher creates it before launch; the wrapper atomically publishes completion. A missing completion is not proof of success: list reports `lost` when the wrapper PID is gone. The launcher passes the record path through the environment; stage2 adds its separately sessioned groups. Stop records its request before ending the command tree and recorded groups, spares the wrapper to record `signal 15`, and refuses finished, lost or identity-mismatched jobs. Finished records are kept 14 days; the default list shows running jobs and the last 24 hours, lost records remain visible until pruned 14 days after start, and `--all` shows all retained records. Start waits at most 10 seconds for both PIDs or records a failed start; the log captures both output streams and is pruned with its record. Distinct IDs and atomic replacement prevent simultaneous jobs from overwriting one another.\n\n",

German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "end_line": 193,
          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree.           "excerpt": "### The review loop (phase 4b)\n\n**Fresh availability-enabled runs (Q-16, ADR 0021):** first run\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-loop <change>`. The runner refreshes Pi's\ncatalog and probes admitted candidates with static input and no tools.\nTimed exclusions are skipped without a call; GLM through OpenCode Go is not\nexcluded (the 2026-10-21 GLM outage covers the Z.ai route only). Paid candidates require known cost, admitted terms and catalog presence.\nReport its timestamped reachable/failed/skipped list and selected stages in\nthe main Claude Code or Codex conversation, then invoke `review-loop <change>\n--availability-reported <id>` with the printed report id. This acknowledges\nthe report; the runner cannot inspect the conversation UI. The external\nreceipt is bound to the worktree, configuration and diff and expires after\n900 seconds. Changed inputs or failed preparation invalidate it. Preparation\nadds one actual call per tested candidate and is no review-quality or billing\nmeasurement. Up to three cheapest reachable paid candidates dynamically fill\nthe Flash swarm; the remaining reachable paid candidates form the ladder.\nExisting snapshots and legacy declarations without the rule retain the\nbehavior below. A run with history cannot be reset by preparation.\n\n**Paid terms expire (ADR 0022, bead coding-harness-abra).** Every\n`modelle_terms` record of a paid model carries `valid_until`, a quoted ISO\ncalendar date the reading is valid through; the following UTC day it is\nexpired, and the judgement reads UTC, never the local calendar. A record\nwithout a usable `valid_until` — missing, not a quoted date, or an impossible\ncalendar date — grants no admission, and the runner never infers, extends or\nrenews a date at runtime. A refusal names the model, says whether the expiry\nis missing, invalid or passed, and names the recorded date once it has\npassed. From seven UTC days before expiry through the expiry day,\npreparation and every round — fresh, legacy or resumed — print a warning\nwith the model id and date, and the round's notes carry it, so the released\nfindings keep it; a warning neither admits nor refuses, an expired reading\nis a skip with its reason, not a warning, and a skipped record with a valid\ndate warns too. A saved selection or a fresh receipt does not keep an\nexpired member admissible: the round is refused before the call, and the\nrun's history stands. Renewal is not the runner's: a reading is introduced\nor renewed by an agent's dated source re-read and a decision pull request\nmerged by the maintainer; where the source states an end date it is\nrecorded, and otherwise a record expires `gelesen` plus 30 calendar days.\nMigrated 2026-10-26 on that rule; both DeepSeek readings carry the\ndocumented 2026-10-25 source re-read and expire 2026-10-31.\n\nAfter implementation and before phase 6, `review-loop` runs one round per\ncall, and the loop runs **until a round is clean — every row of a round\ndecided and none accepted (ADR 0021).** Round 1 is the **free swarm**: a\nforced live catalog refresh (`pi update --models` before `pi --list-models`,\nno stale cache listed) discovers the models the `opencode-go` provider offers,\nand the `free_stage` rule in `model-endpoints.yaml` — provider, id suffix,\nincludes, excludes — selects the members; they review in parallel, each with\nno tools, from a scratch directory, and their only input is the\nimplementation diff: bounded hunks of source and test code against the merge\nbase with `origin/main`, uncommitted and untracked code included. The catalog\nis a live intermediary (`pi.dev`): the check proves which catalog was read,\nnot what OpenCode Go bills. The prompt carries the implementation diff up to\nthe shared bound of `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES` (4000 lines); a cut, whether by\nthat bound or by the free stage's own file or total limits, is recorded in the\nround, and a round over a cut diff never counts as clean (R-12, R-15). When\nevery free member fails with a rate-limit (429) or unavailability error, ",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: **Option 2 — State-first JSON/JSONL, single kit manifest, and shared script primitives.**\n\n### 1. State-first machine persistence (`coding-harness-5ane.11`, aligned with `coding-harness-oebl`)\n\n1. All mutable orchestration state — review-loop rounds, consumed/retired stages, Phase-6 verdicts, lane state (`lanes.py`), detached job state (`jobs.py`), and attempt state — MUST persist canonically in schema-validated, file-locked JSON/JSONL files.\n2. Human-facing Markdown (`loop.md`, released blocks in `findings.md`, `plans/INDEX.md`, `gate-catalog.md`) is deterministically rendered from structured state (`machine-rendered`), never parsed back via regexes to recover control state.\n3. Structured runner event/audit logs follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI JSONL contract established in `coding-harness-oebl` (one producer, one read interface, many readers; plain files only, no visual dashboards per `AGENTS.md`).\n4. A bounded dual-read fallback handles in-flight `loop.md` files during migration and is removed once active changes roll over.\n\n### 2. Single kit manifest & dependency-verified export (`coding-harness-5ane.10`, `coding-harness-5ane.7`)\n\n1. Retire `scripts/export/manifest.yaml`; maintain **one** declarative kit manifest (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`, aligned with `feat/central-config`) as the single source of truth for what travels with the kit vs. stays repository-local (`bestand`).\n2. `scripts/kit/probe.py` MUST verify static import closure for every exported Python script so missing dependencies (such as `scripts/bead_render.py`) fail immediately at manifest check time rather than at runtime in a target repository.\n3. Drive `DECKEL` in `scripts/kit/probe.py` monotonically from `44` to `0` by isolating repository-inventory tests into `bestand` and fixing genuine portability gaps in `mechanismus` tests.\n\n### 3. Shared script primitives (`coding-harness-5ane.12`)\n\n1. Extract and standardize three leaf primitives under `scripts/` (requiring Python 3.12+ stdlib + `PyYAML` only):\n   * `_yaml_strict.py`: single duplicate-key-rejecting `SafeLoader` and BOM/CRLF-safe frontmatter span reader;\n   * `_fs_atomic.py`: single symlink-safe (`lstat` check) temp-file + `fsync` + `os.replace` writer;\n   * `_git_exec.py`: single `GIT_*`/`LC_ALL`-sanitized git subprocess runner with explicit timeouts.\n2. All new and refactored scripts MUST import these shared primitives rather than introducing local copies, enforced by an AST/import guard test.\n\n",

          "end_line": 5739,
          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "citation": "docs/testing.md::How a test is written",
          "end_line": 56,
          "excerpt": "## How a test is written\n\n- **Stand-ins, never live calls.** A test that drives the runner puts small\n  programs on `PATH` in place of the model tools. They record their\n  arguments, environment and input, print canned output and contact nothing.\n  Credentials are synthetic. No test reads the maintainer's denylist, secrets\n  or loop records.\n- **Each new test names its fault.** Its docstring says which fault the test\n  was red on (`Planted fault: …`); this is the convention for new tests, and\n  older ones are not all rewritten. A test that has never been red is a test of\n  nothing.\n- **Doctrine tests.** Some tests read the workflow's own documents and prompts\n  and pin a rule there. Each one checks its fault on a planted copy of the\n  text, so the test is shown to catch the drift it guards.\n- **Mutation names.** A test that proves a gate goes red carries the fact in\n  its name (`…_goes_red…`, `…_refuses…`, `…_is_caught…`). A name moves with a\n  rename, a comment does not. The gate ratchet counts these names.\n- **A test reads only what travels**, or it skips with its reason. Otherwise\n  the kit probe turns it red in a repository that lacks the file.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/testing.md",
          "reference": "How a test is written",
