          "end_line": 563,
          "excerpt": "def test_records_are_schema_validated_and_atomic(state: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: an invalid or partial record becomes visible, or concurrent updates overwrite each other\n    (criterion 19).\"\"\"\n    job_id = jobs.new_job_id()\n    path = record_path(job_id)\n    good = jobs.new_record(job_id, [\"echo\", \"hi\"], \"/work\", str(state / f\"{job_id}.log\"))\n    for broken in (\n        {**good, \"schema\": True},\n        {**good, \"schema\": 1.0},\n        {**good, \"state\": \"sleeping\"},\n        {**good, \"command\": []},\n        {**good, \"groups\": [{\"pgid\": \"x\", \"pid\": 1, \"start\": None}]},\n        {k: v for k, v in good.items() if k != \"log\"},\n        {**good, \"extra\": 1},\n    ):\n        with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n            jobs.write_record(path, broken)\n        assert not path.exists(), \"an invalid record was published\"\n    jobs.write_record(path, good)\n    before = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    real_fsync = os.fsync\n\n    def failing_fsync(_fd: int) -> None:\n        raise OSError(\"disk\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", failing_fsync)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError, match=\"disk\"):\n        jobs.write_record(path, {**good, \"state\": \"running\"})\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", real_fsync)\n    assert path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == before, \"a failed write left a partial record\"\n    assert sorted(p.name for p in state.iterdir()) == [path.name]  # no temporary file remains\n    path.write_text(before[: len(before) // 2], encoding=\"utf-8\")  # a truncated record is refused, never repaired\n    with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n        jobs.read_record(path)\n    path.write_text(before, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    def add(n: int):\n        return lambda record: record[\"groups\"].append({\"pgid\": n, \"pid\": n, \"start\": None})\n\n    threads = [threading.Thread(target=jobs.update_record, args=(path, add(n))) for n in range(1, 9)]\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.start()\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.join()\n    assert sorted(g[\"pgid\"] for g in jobs.read_record(path)[\"groups\"]) == list(range(1, 9))\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_shared_format_preserves_runner_bytes_and_midnight() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 2. Planted fault: changed metadata, a different suffix, or a midnight span without its end date.\"\"\"\n    end = START + dt.timedelta(seconds=600)\n    same_day = time_records.format_entry(START, end, 600, \"implement\", 1, \"flash\", \"glm-5.3-flash\", \"accepted\")\n    assert same_day == (\n        \"2026-10-20 10:00:00–10:10:00 UTC, 600 s — implement · attempt 1 · route flash · \"\n        \"model glm-5.3-flash · accepted · measured by the runner\"\n    )\n    # The named outcome is the only difference between the two verdicts' lines.\n    rejected = time_records.format_entry(START, end, 600, \"implement\", 1, \"flash\", \"glm-5.3-flash\", \"rejected\")\n    assert rejected == same_day.replace(\"accepted\", \"rejected\")\n    # A span across midnight carries the end's date; a same-day span carries none.\n    midnight_start = dt.datetime(2026, 10, 20, 23, 59, 30, tzinfo=dt.UTC)\n    midnight_end = dt.datetime(2026, 10, 21, 0, 0, 16, tzinfo=dt.UTC)\n    across = time_records.format_entry(\n        midnight_start, midnight_end, 45, \"implement\", 2, \"flash\", \"glm-5.3-flash\", \"rejected\"\n    )\n    assert across == (\n        \"2026-10-20 23:59:30–2026-10-21 00:00:16 UTC, 45 s — implement · attempt 2 · route flash · \"\n        \"model glm-5.3-flash · rejected · measured by the runner\"\n    )\n    # The fixed line survives the shared parser with every field intact, and prose stays unread.\n    assert time_records.parse_entry(across) == time_records.Record(\n        seconds=45, verb=\"implement\", attempt=2, route=\"flash\", model=\"glm-5.3-flash\", result=\"rejected\"\n    )\n    assert time_records.parse_entry(same_day + \" (approx)\") is None\n    assert time_records.parse_entry(\"2026-10-20 10:00–10:10 UTC, 600 s\") is None\n",

          "excerpt": "def _record_lines(record: str) -> list[tuple[str, bool]]:\n    \"\"\"Each line of the record, and whether it is the reviewer's words - not the runner's or the orchestrator's.\n\n    The runner writes a round as its heading, then a table or one statement and, when the answer was not\n    only six-cell rows, the note `NOT_ROWS_NOTE` and the rest of the answer as it came. The lines after the\n    note, up to the next round heading, are the reviewer's; every other line is the record's own. A line\n    of the reviewer is quoted when written, so it cannot become a round heading.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines = []\n    reviewer = False\n    for line in record.splitlines():\n        if ROUND_HEADING.match(line):\n            reviewer = False\n        elif reviewer and FROM_LINE.fullmatch(line):\n            # Every reviewer line is quoted, so an unquoted `From <member>:` is the runner's: it closes one\n            # member's words and names the next member's (DL-B-3).\n            reviewer = False\n        elif not reviewer and line.strip() == NOT_ROWS_NOTE:\n            lines.append((line, False))\n            reviewer = True\n            continue\n        lines.append((line, reviewer))\n    return lines\n",

          "excerpt": "def record_rows(record: str, *, strict: bool = False) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"The loop rows of the record: every table line of its own whose first cell is a loop id.\n\n    Only the record's own lines are read, never the reviewer's words, which are carried as they came: a\n    table line the reviewer wrote is not a row the orchestrator has to decide, whatever its first cell says.\n\n    Nine cells are known. A `|` the orchestrator typed into `Status` makes a tenth; the cells between the\n    reviewer and the last one are that reason, each pipe escaped. A line with a loop id and fewer cells\n    than a row has is not skipped, which would let the release delete it with the record: it is refused,\n    by its id. Triage uses `strict` to refuse any non-nine-cell row before editing;\n    the compatibility reader for other verbs still accepts typed Status pipes.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    in_table = False\n    for line, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n        if reviewer:\n            in_table = False\n            continue\n        cells = split_row(line)\n        if strict:\n            # Check table syntax before filtering loop IDs: split_row deliberately returns None\n            # for missing boundary pipes, which must never hide a damaged runner-owned row.\n            first = _PIPE.split(line.strip().lstrip(\"|\"), maxsplit=1)[0].strip()\n            table_line = (\n                line.lstrip().startswith(\"|\")\n                or (in_table and bool(line.strip()))\n                or (\"|\" in line and (LOOP_ID.fullmatch(first) or first == ROW_COLUMNS[0]))\n            )\n            in_table = bool(table_line)\n            if table_line and (cells is None or len(cells) != len(ROW_COLUMNS)):\n                count = \"missing boundary pipe\" if cells is None else f\"{len(cells)} cells\"\n                raise Refused(\n                    f\"the loop record has a malformed loop row/table line ({count}; \"\n                    f\"{len(ROW_COLUMNS)} cells are needed); mend it, nothing has been written.\"\n                )\n        if not cells or not LOOP_ID.fullmatch(cells[0]):\n            continue\n        if len(cells) < len(ROW_COLUMNS) or (strict and len(cells) != len(ROW_COLUMNS)):\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"the loop record has a line for {cells[0]} that is not a loop row \"\n                f\"({len(cells)} cells; {len(ROW_COLUMNS)} are needed); mend it, nothing has been deleted.\"\n            )\n        if (\n            len(cells) > len(ROW_COLUMNS)\n            and cells[7].strip().lower().startswith((\"taken\", \"fixed\"))\n            and not marks_a_test(cells[-1])\n        ):\n ",

      "statement": "Today's defence against reviewer prose becoming control state is two-sided, and only one side is removed by a JSON record: `_record_lines` classifies each line as the reviewer's or the runner's (a quoted `|`-row or an unquoted heading is not the reviewer's) and `quote_reviewer` re-quotes reviewer text on the way out, while `record_rows` additionally refuses malformed rows (missing boundary pipe, wrong cell count, a moved `Broke a test` mark) instead of skipping them. A structured record removes the parse-side refusals, but the render side still writes reviewer words into findings.md, where the released-block readers (`released_digest`, `read_state`, `highest_assigned_round`) look for the runner's own line prefixes."

The lines after the\n    note, up to the next round heading, are the reviewer's; every other line is the record's own.           "excerpt": "def replace_record(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write the record whole or not at all: a temporary file in its directory, then an atomic rename\n    (`Path.replace`, which is `os.replace`).\n\n    `Path.write_text` truncates first and writes after; a write that fails between the two keeps a\n    record cut short, and the record is the only copy of its rounds (DL-A-4 of the deep review). The\n    temporary file never outlives a failed write.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    handle, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\", dir=path.parent)\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(handle, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n            stream.write(text)\n            stream.flush()\n            # Reconciliation also replaces findings.md: retain its permissions instead of\n            # installing mkstemp's private mode. Fresh external records keep that private mode.\n            if path.exists():\n                os.fchmod(stream.fileno(), path.stat().st_mode & 0o7777)\n            os.fsync(stream.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`. The lock is advisory, held by the open descriptor, and\n    a descriptor dies with its process - so a crashed run leaves no lock behind to break the next.\n    Supersession holds its own and every selected worktree's lock in one deterministic order, so it\n    cannot bypass a normal user of either record (bead coding-harness-e82i, criterion 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    path = record_base() / f\"{key}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"another run holds the loop record `{key}`; one runner at a time\") from error\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "def holding_supersession(change: str, root: Path) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Serialize release and supersession across this repository's worktrees.\"\"\"\n    common = os.fsdecode(run_git(root, \"rev-parse\", \"--git-common-dir\").stdout).strip()\n    common_path = (root / common).resolve()\n    digest = hashlib.sha256(str(common_path).encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()[:16]\n    path = record_base() / f\"supersession-{digest}-{change}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            handle.seek(0)\n            holder = handle.read().strip() or \"unknown worktree\"\n            raise Refused(f\"supersession lock for {change} is held by {holder}; nothing is changed\") from error\n        try:\n            handle.seek(0)\n            handle.truncate()\n            handle.write(record_key(change, root))\n            handle.flush()\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py::Store",
          "end_line": 480,
          "excerpt": "class Store:\n    \"\"\"One change's research state directory.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, directory, *, scrub: Callable[[str], str] | None = None):\n        self.directory = Path(directory)\n        self._scrub = scrub\n        self._lock_fd = None\n\n    # -- placement --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def assert_outside(self, *forbidden, home=None):\n        \"\"\"Refuse a store inside (or equal to) any directory a model, the worktree or git may see.\n\n        ``home`` is the real home directory Claude research processes inherit;           "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`.           "excerpt": "def holding_supersession(change: str, root: Path) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Serialize release and supersession across this repository's worktrees.\"\"\"\n    common = os.fsdecode(run_git(root, \"rev-parse\", \"--git-common-dir\").stdout).strip()\n    common_path = (root / common).resolve()\n    digest = hashlib.sha256(str(common_path).encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()[:16]\n    path = record_base() / f\"supersession-{digest}-{change}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            handle.seek(0)\n            holder = handle.read().strip() or \"unknown worktree\"\n            raise Refused(f\"supersession lock for {change} is held by {holder}; nothing is changed\") from error\n        try:\n            handle.seek(0)\n            handle.truncate()\n            handle.write(record_key(change, root))\n            handle.flush()\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_findings(text: str, *, change: str, path: str) -> Parsed:\n    \"\"\"The eligible rows, the outside tables and the gaps of one findings.md, read by ``scan``.\"\"\"\n    blocks: list[Block] = []\n    gaps: list[Gap] = []\n    calls: list[CallLine] = []\n    groups: dict[tuple[str, int], OutsideTable] = {}\n    section = Section()\n    last_release_heading = 0\n    last_phase6_heading = 0\n\n    def gap(row_id: str | None, position: int, reason: str) -> None:\n        gaps.append(Gap(path, row_id, f\"line {position}: {reason}\"))\n\n    def outside(position: int, *, grouped: str | None = None) -> None:\n        # criterion 18: a finding table under a heading that is not counted stands\n        # outside the count with its heading of any level; \"headingless\" only\n        # before the first heading (F6-2).\n        if grouped is not None:\n            key = (grouped, 0)\n        elif section.heading is None:\n            key = (\"headingless tables\", 0)\n        else:\n            key = next(((label, 0) for prefix, label in GROUPED_OUTSIDE if section.heading.startswith(prefix)), None)\n            key = key or (section.heading, section.position)\n        group = groups.get(key)\n        if group is None:\n            groups[key] = OutsideTable(key[0], position, 1, change, path)\n        else:\n            group.rows += 1\n\n    for line in scan(text):\n        position = line.position\n   ",
